transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… what brings me in is mostly that I’m having a really hard time keeping my attention on things I know are important. Like at work, I’ll be in a safety briefing or going over a plan review, and I’ll start out really trying to listen — I mean, I know those things matter, I’m a construction manager, missing details can turn into real problems — but within a few minutes my head is already somewhere else.

It’s like I’m standing there looking like I’m paying attention, but mentally I’m off thinking about three other job problems at once. A crew issue, a schedule problem, something with materials, whatever it is. And then I realize I’ve missed part of what someone said, or I’ll catch myself later thinking, “I should have caught that.” It’s frustrating because I’m not trying to blow it off. I’m trying hard, and it still happens.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself moving around when you need to stay still, like during meetings or when sitting for long periods?

Yeah, definitely. Meetings are probably the clearest example. If everybody else is sitting there through the whole thing, I’m usually the one who’s up at some point — getting coffee, walking to the back of the room, stepping outside like I need to check on something, or making some excuse to move around.

Sometimes I’ll tell myself it’s work-related, like, “I should go check that text,” or “I need to see if the crew is ready,” but if I’m being honest, a lot of the time I just can’t stand sitting there that long. I feel like I have to get up. Even if I know I’m supposed to stay put, it’s like my body is pushing me to move.
Do you often feel excessive worry or anxiety about things, even when there isn't an immediate problem, like worrying about things going wrong at work even when everything seems under control?

I’m not sure I’d call it worry exactly. I mean, in construction there’s always stuff that can go wrong, so my mind is on things a lot — schedules, people showing up, whether something got missed — but I don’t know if that’s anxiety like you mean.

It’s more like… if something pops into my head, I’ll think about it, and sometimes I probably overthink it, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there scared for no reason when everything’s fine. I don’t know. I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed excessive worry as the main thing. It’s more that my mind jumps around to whatever might need attention.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even if just for a few days a week?

I don’t think so, not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I have days where I’m tired or irritated, and there are days where work has beaten me up and I come home kind of flat, but I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless or like I’ve lost interest in everything.

Like, if I get a chance to do something I actually enjoy, I can still enjoy it. It’s more that sometimes by the time I get to it, I’m already worn out or my mind is still spinning from the day. But I don’t sit around thinking there’s no point or that nothing is enjoyable anymore. At least, I haven’t really noticed that as a pattern.
Do you find yourself feeling noticeably tense, even in situations where others might not see a problem, like during routine tasks or when things are going as planned at work?

I don’t know that I’d say “tense,” exactly. I mean, I can get keyed up at work, but that feels more like the job is active and there are moving parts, not like I’m sitting there tight for no reason when things are fine.

If everything’s actually going according to plan, I don’t usually notice myself being physically tense like that — like shoulders clenched or stomach in knots or whatever. I might still be thinking through the next thing or checking what’s coming up, but I wouldn’t describe it as feeling noticeably tense. At least not that I’ve really paid attention to.
Have you noticed any specific areas of your life, like work, hobbies, or time with family and friends, where you’ve lost interest or don’t get the same satisfaction out of them anymore?

Not really, no. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in anything across the board. Work can wear me down, sure, and sometimes by the end of the day I don’t have much left in the tank, so if someone asks me to go do something or if there’s something I normally like, I might put it off or not feel up for it right then.

But that feels more like being tired or mentally used up, not like I don’t care about those things anymore. If I actually get started, or if I’m in the right mood, I can still enjoy stuff. Same with family or friends — I don’t feel like I’m detached from them or like I don’t get anything out of being around them. It’s more just… my energy and attention are all over the place sometimes, so it might look like I’m not interested, but I don’t think that’s really what’s going on.

Have you noticed any days where you feel down or unmotivated even when you're not physically tired, or where you don't get satisfaction out of things that usually make you feel good, like seeing family or finishing a task at work?

I’m not sure I can point to that, honestly. I mean, I have days where I don’t want to do anything, but when I really think about it, there’s usually some reason — like I’m drained from the day, or I’ve been running around, or I’ve had too much on my plate mentally. It’s hard for me to separate “unmotivated” from just being worn out or scattered.

As far as not getting satisfaction from things, I don’t think so. If I finish something at work, especially if it was a headache and I finally got it done, I can still feel good about that. And with family, I still like seeing them. Sometimes I’m distracted or it takes me a while to settle into it, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there feeling nothing or like it doesn’t matter.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed days like that where everything should be fine and I’m still just down for no reason, or where the things that normally feel good suddenly don’t. If it happens, I guess I haven’t recognized it as a pattern.
Have you ever felt down or lost interest in things even when you’re not stressed or tired, like on your day off or after a good night’s sleep?

Yeah… I mean, thinking about a day off or after actually sleeping well, I don’t really notice that kind of thing. If I’ve got a free day and I’m not wiped out, I usually can get into something, even if it takes me a while to decide what I’m doing or I waste half the morning kind of puttering around.

I wouldn’t say I wake up rested and then still feel down for no clear reason, or like nothing sounds good. It’s more that sometimes I don’t start things well, or I get stuck deciding, and then the day can get away from me. But if I end up seeing family, or doing something I like, or even just getting something done around the house, I can still feel pretty good about it.

So no, not really in the way you’re asking. If I’m not stressed or tired, I don’t think I’m usually down or uninterested. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you ever felt down or lost interest in things even when you’re not stressed or tired, like on your day off or after a good night’s sleep?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, if I’m really being honest, I can have a day off where I don’t get much done and I kind of sit around longer than I meant to, and then I’ll feel annoyed with myself. But that’s not exactly feeling down out of nowhere, if that makes sense.

Like, if I actually slept well and I’m not under the gun with work or family stuff, I can usually enjoy things. I might take forever to pick what I’m doing, or I’ll start one thing and drift into another, and then suddenly it’s noon and I haven’t done the thing I planned. But if I go see family, or watch something I like, or finish a project around the house, I still get something out of it.

So I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest or that nothing feels good. It’s more like I get stalled, and then I get frustrated because I wasted time. But I haven’t really noticed that thing where I’m rested and everything’s fine and I’m still just low or empty.
